title: Avoidable copies of large objects
summary: Passing, returning, or assigning large containers and objects by value when moves or references would avoid copying.
rationale: C++ value semantics are powerful, but accidental copies can dominate CPU and memory behavior.

detection.notes: Detect large parameter-by-value, missing std::move, or range-for copies.

impact.notes: Impact increases in hot paths, large inputs, high-concurrency services, build pipelines, or repeated request paths.

remediation.guidance: Use const references, moves, views, emplacement, or explicit ownership transfer where appropriate.
remediation.tradeoffs: References and moves can obscure ownership; prefer simple value semantics for small types.

pattern.title: Avoidable copies of large objects
